china-peking-1921:p0495_1.rationale: Lists the gilds and organizations belonging to the Peking Chamber of Commerce with member stores and chamber and board representatives; this is the organisation of a commercial association.

china-peking-1921:p0506_1.rationale: Classifies stores by monthly income under the municipal tax regulations, as the basis of a store tax assessment.

china-peking-1921:p0507_1.rationale: Gives the monthly tax payable by each class of store under the Peking municipal tax regulations.

china-peking-1921:p0509_1.rationale: A list of book titles from which professional story tellers draw their stories. The content is textual and concerns recreation and performance.
review_questions: Vocabulary has no tag for storytelling or traditional oral performance; consider proposing one.

china-peking-1921:p0509_2.rationale: Maps each day of the Chinese month to the temple holding its market. The content is textual scheduling and covers recreation and commerce at temples.
review_questions: No tag fits temple markets or fairs; consider proposing one.

china-peking-1921:p0509_3.rationale: Inventory of billiard rooms with counts of billiard tables and bowling alleys by city district, an amusement-venue listing.
review_questions: Could sports-organisations-and-facilities fit better if billiards counts as sport?

china-peking-1921:p0514_1.rationale: Annual tax income drawn from prostitutes and brothels in Peking, 1912-1917, so it concerns regulated sex work and its taxation.

china-peking-1921:p0518_1.rationale: 1917 statistics of the Door of Hope refuge for prostitutes: admissions, departures, deaths, inmates, expenses and government funding.
review_questions: Does the vocabulary need a tag for rescue homes for prostitutes?

china-peking-1921:p0520_1.rationale: Police census of houses and people classed as very poor in each police district, with persons per house and percent of population.

china-peking-1921:p0521_1.rationale: Attendance of men, women and children at gruel kitchens run by police, military guard and Ching Chao Ying, with percentages by centre; this is food relief for the poor.
